title: 2022 surplus allocation and COVID-relief fund reallocation
subtitle: Also: trail and retaining wall repairs, new aerial fire truck, museum review, and a church community centre grant request.
overview: Council approved how to use the 2022 surplus. COVID-related deficits were covered with federal and provincial grant funds, $500,000 went to the Winter Control Reserve, and the remaining non-COVID surplus was split among three reserves {{vote:m9}}. A first-quarter projection shows the 2023 tax base on track to break even {{vote:m10}}.

Council also moved up to $400,000 of leftover COVID-relief funds into two uses: $200,000 back to the Uptown improvement program and $200,000 for one-time support to affiliates and key cultural institutions {{vote:m11}}. Council approved $458,000 for trail and retaining wall rehabilitation {{vote:m12}} and the purchase of a new aerial fire truck for $1,909,679.04 including unrecoverable HST {{vote:m13}}.

A request from All Saints' Anglican Church for a $120,000 grant toward a new community centre did not move forward. A motion asking staff to study its economic, equity, inclusion and programming impacts failed {{vote:m14}}, so no grant or staff report was approved. Council also held an informal public meeting on general zoning by-law updates, which will return to Council later.

decisions.detail: Council applied grant funds to the 2022 COVID deficit, put $500,000 into the Winter Control Reserve and allocated the remaining $378,790 among the RIM Park Investment, Tax Rate Stabilization and Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment reserves.

Council reallocated up to $400,000 in surplus COVID-relief funds, split evenly between the Uptown CIP and one-time support for affiliates and key cultural institutions, after staff's proposed split was revised from $250,000 and $150,000.
Council approved the 2023 implementation plan and released $458,000 from the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve Fund for trail resurfacing and retaining wall replacements.
Council awarded RFQ23-04 to City View Specialty Vehicles for a total of $1,909,679.04 and approved a $305,000 reserve transfer.
Council accepted a projected break-even tax base and an Enterprise surplus of about $0.9M, and asked staff for a follow-up projection in fall 2023.

decisions.item: All Saints' Anglican Church grant request
decisions.detail: A motion to have staff investigate the economic, equity, inclusion and programming impacts of the church's $120,000 request failed {{vote:m14}}.
Council approved the museum review report and committed to continue supporting the museum's work in building community relationships.

debate: On the COVID-relief fund, one councillor argued for giving more to arts and cultural groups because requests last year were more than double the funding available. Staff said the Uptown money is one-time funding meant to last, and any change would need firm figures in a motion.

Staff said accessibility is a new focus for the Uptown program, but its structure is set through a provincial process and is difficult to change. They said there was enough funding to cover a strong first year.

The church's representatives said the city has no neighbourhood community centres, which leaves lower-income areas without affordable space. They said the new centre's community space would be secular and open to all, and that they had approached the Region and were pointed to its Upstream fund.

Councillors raised concerns about fairness, since the church sold property to fund its project, and about setting a precedent for funding faith-based facilities. Others asked about comfort among equity-deserving groups and a preference for public delivery of community programs.

Staff said Albert McCormick Community Centre is being enhanced, but it is a long walk from the church's area. They said a broader review of community versus centralized models would fit the recreation master plan starting in 2024, and that a report on the request would take several weeks of staff time and return in the fall.
